children: Coffee Holding reported third-quarter results for the period ended July 31, 2026, with net sales of $21.686 million and gross profit of $5.424 million. The company posted net income of $1.993 million, or $0.35 per share basic and diluted, compared with a net loss in the prior-year quarter. Management cited volatile green coffee markets, favorable inventory positioning, tariff refunds and trading gains as principal drivers of improved profitability.
Net sales: $21,686,262 for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (down 9.3% from $23,910,514 in Q3 2025).
Gross profit: $5,424,131 for the three months ended July 31, 2026; gross margin 25.0% (vs. $2,255,028 and 9.4% in Q3 2025).
Cost of sales: $16,262,131 for Q3 2026 (75.0% of net sales) compared with $21,655,486 (90.6% of net sales) in Q3 2025.
Operating income: $2,324,330 from operations for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (compared with an operating loss of $1,095,151 in Q3 2025).
Net income and EPS: Net income of $1,993,438; basic and diluted income per share $0.35 for the three months ended July 31, 2026 (vs. net loss of $1,205,413 and $(0.21) per share in Q3 2025).

Market pricing response: Company reduced prices and ran promotions for wholesale roasted customers and lowered prices for wholesale green coffee customers in response to a sustained decline in green coffee prices during the quarter.
Inventory positioning: Management attributes improved margins to a favorable inventory position established earlier in the year when green coffee prices declined significantly.

Tariff refunds and trading: Tariff refunds recognized during the quarter and a net gain on trading activity materially contributed to gross profit and earnings; tariff refunds added approximately $0.06 per share to quarterly earnings.

Customer retention and business development: Company retained its wholesale roasted customer base after foregoing most tariff charges in 2025 and reported securing significant new business expected to support revenue and margin expansion into 2027.
Operational consistency: Selling and administrative expenses and overall operating expenses remained generally consistent with historical levels despite market volatility.
